correctness.rationale: The query universe is Boolean colour-equality tests (v,a), not multiclass answers. An isolated vertex gives one bit of online depth, a tree with m vertices exactly m: an adaptive root query determines a color with two nonempty branches, then descendants can be queried against one of their two parent-allowed colors. For each cycle C_ell, the explicit complete tree achieves ell-1 levels, and the number of proper colorings 2^ell+2(-1)^ell, with colour-symmetric positive root branch size at most (2^ell+2)/3 < 2^(ell-1), precludes depth ell. The same cycle tree extends to attached trees, giving ell+m-1 for unicyclic connected graphs. Products of nonempty graph concept classes on disjoint query universes have additive Ldim; monotonicity under deletion of edge constraints and a spanning subgraph comprising nu disjoint cycles plus isolated vertices gives Ldim(C3(G)) <= n-nu. For pseudoforests additivity and exact component dimensions attain the bound. If G is not 3-colorable, its class is empty and the bound remains valid. Independently computed minimax dimensions for seven small path/cycle/unicyclic examples and the exact packing bound.
residual_risks: The upper bound need not be tight on multiply cyclic graphs; proof of arbitrary-graph bound derives from a cycle-only theorem plus standard monotonicity/additivity but has a broad parameter domain.
Finite examples do not prove all graph classes; general proof is constructive.

value.rationale: Vertex-disjoint cycle packing is a natural obstruction to online identifiability of a proper 3-colouring via binary equality queries. The sharp graph-wide parameter bound and complete exact dimension on all pseudoforests connect online learning to topological cycle structure; the iff forest criterion is a useful structural classification. The result does not claim every graph saturates the bound or that a small finite computation is itself an infinite theorem.
